Based on the ISO 45001 standards documentation, you must apply the **hierarchy of controls in this specific order** before considering PPE:

## Hierarchy of Controls (Clause 8.1.2)

| Priority | Control Measure |
|----------|---------------|
| **1st** | **Eliminate** the hazard |
| **2nd** | **Substitute** with less hazardous processes or materials |
| **3rd** | **Engineering controls** and **work reorganization** |
| **4th** | **Administrative controls** (including training) |
| **5th (last)** | **Personal protective equipment (PPE)** — only when adequate |

## Key Supporting Requirements

- **Clause 6.1.4** requires that planning actions to address risks must **consider the hierarchy of controls**
- **Clause 10.2** mandates that corrective actions also be determined **"in line with the hierarchy of controls"**

## The Bottom Line

PPE is explicitly the **last resort** in ISO 45001. Your plant manager's default approach of "buy more PPE" for every risk violates the standard's fundamental requirement to work through elimination, substitution, engineering controls, and administrative measures **first**.
